subproblems.title: Two unit orientations of the same n-plane differ by a sign
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let Q be a linear subspace of ℝ^P and let v, w ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P n: continuous linear functionals on n-covectors, ⟨α, v⟩ = v(α)). If v and w are both unit orientations of Q (IsUnitOrientationOf v Q and IsUnitOrientationOf w Q: for some orthonormal families τ, τ' : Fin n → ℝ^P spanning Q, v(α) = ±α(τ) and w(α) = ±α(τ') for all n-covectors α), then w = v or w = −v.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (v w : MultiVector P n) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), IsUnitOrientationOf v Q → IsUnitOrientationOf w Q → w = v ∨ w = -v
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 (F3) of the supplied proof of the selected theorem (Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(1), chapter-06.txt lines 755–756, stated there without proof; an n-vector τ₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ τₙ pairs with an n-covector α as α(τ₁, …, τₙ), Simon 6.1). This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.rsdic_unitOrientation_eq_or_eq_neg (DAG node root.regular_set_dense-a1.integer_combination-a1.orientation_sign-a1, candidate fe95347), reused at its byte-identical frozen type; the argument below is the one formalized there. Notation: for a family σ : Fin n → ℝ^P and an n-covector α, α(σ) := α(σ₁, …, σₙ).
1. Unfolding the hypotheses. There are orthonormal families τ, τ' : Fin n → ℝ^P with span(range τ) = Q = span(range τ') and signs ε, ε' ∈ {1, −1} such that v(α) = ε·α(τ) and w(α) = ε'·α(τ') for every n-covector α (one sign for all α, as in the definition).
2. Orthonormal bases of Q. Each τ_i lies in span(range τ) = Q and each τ'_i lies in Q. Let t, t' : Fin n → Q be the same vectors regarded as elements of the inner product space Q (with the inner product of ℝ^P). The inclusion Q → ℝ^P is a linear isometry, so t and t' are orthonormal, hence linearly independent. They span Q: every y ∈ Q = span(range τ) can be written y = Σ_i c_i τ_i, and then y = Σ_i c_i t_i in Q; likewise for t'. Hence t and t' are orthonormal bases b and b' of Q indexed by Fin n (Mathlib OrthonormalBasis.mk), with b_i = τ_i and b'_i = τ'_i as vectors of ℝ^P.
3. The change-of-basis determinant. Let d := det_b(b') (b.toBasis.det b'), the determinant of the matrix expressing b' in the basis b. This matrix is orthogonal because both bases are orthonormal, so d ∈ {1, −1} (Mathlib OrthonormalBasis.det_to_matrix_orthonormalBasis_real).
4. Comparison of α(τ') and α(τ). Fix an n-covector α and let α_Q be its restriction to Q, i.e. the alternating n-linear form on Q obtained by composing α with the inclusion Q → ℝ^P in every slot (α.toAlternatingMap.compLinearMap Q.subtype). Since Q has the basis b with n elements, every alternating n-linear form on Q is a scalar multiple of det_b; precisely α_Q = α_Q(b)·det_b (Mathlib AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det). Evaluating at b' and using b_i = τ_i, b'_i = τ'_i: α(τ') = α_Q(b') = α_Q(b)·det_b(b') = d·α(τ). The number d does not depend on α.
5. Conclusion. For every n-covector α, using step 4 and ε² = 1: w(α) = ε'·α(τ') = ε'·d·α(τ) = (ε ε' d)·(ε·α(τ)) = s·v(α), where s := ε ε' d ∈ {1, −1}. If s = 1 then w(α) = v(α) for all α, so w = v by extensionality of continuous linear maps; if s = −1 then w(α) = −v(α) = (−v)(α) for all α, so w = −v. For n = 0 the same argument applies verbatim (τ and τ' are the empty family, Q = {0}, b and b' are the empty basis and d = 1). ∎
proof_key_steps: The orthonormal families τ, τ' spanning Q are orthonormal bases b, b' of Q.
det_b(b') = ±1 because the change-of-basis matrix between orthonormal bases is orthogonal.
Every alternating n-form on Q is a multiple of det_b, so α(τ') = det_b(b')·α(τ) for every n-covector α.
Hence w = (εε'det_b(b'))·v with εε'det_b(b') ∈ {±1}, i.e. w = v or w = −v.

subproblems.title: An a.e. identity of weighted orientations yields the integer combination of the represented currents
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, let R₁ = (M₁, θ₁, ξ₁), R₂ = (M₂, θ₂, ξ₂), R = (M, θ, ξ) be IMReps in U (Simon Ch. 6, 3.1) and p₁, p₂ ∈ ℤ. Suppose that for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ ℝ^P (Hⁿ = μHE[n]) the n-vectors satisfy 1_M(x)θ(x)ξ(x) = p₁1_{M₁}(x)θ₁(x)ξ₁(x) + p₂1_{M₂}(x)θ₂(x)ξ₂(x). Then for every test form ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (ω : TestFormOn U n) we have τ(R)(ω) = p₁τ(R₁)(ω) + p₂τ(R₂)(ω), where τ(R)(ω) = R.action ω = ∫_M θ(x)⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ(x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R₁ R₂ R : IMRep U n) (p₁ p₂ : ℤ), (∀ᵐ x ∂μHE[n], R.carrier.indicator (fun y => (R.mult y : ℝ) • R.orient y) x = (p₁ : ℝ) • R₁.carrier.indicator (fun y => (R₁.mult y : ℝ) • R₁.orient y) x + (p₂ : ℝ) • R₂.carrier.indicator (fun y => (R₂.mult y : ℝ) • R₂.orient y) x) → ∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, R.action (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) = (p₁ : ℝ) * R₁.action (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) + (p₂ : ℝ) * R₂.action (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 9 of the supplied proof of the selected theorem (the representation of S − T: all integrands are integrable, being bounded by θ·sup|ω|·1_{tsupport ω}, and the integral is linear), for a general integer combination (Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(1), chapter-06.txt lines 755–756: p₁T₁ + p₂T₂). The selected theorem uses it with p₁ = 1, p₂ = −1. This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.rsdic_imrep_action_int_combination (DAG node root.regular_set_dense-a1.integer_combination-a1.combination_action-a1, candidate faacb9c), reused at its byte-identical frozen type; the argument below is the one formalized there. Notation: μ := μHE[n]; for an IMRep R' = (M', θ', ξ') in U put F_{R'}(x) := 1_{M'}(x)θ'(x)ξ'(x) ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^P), so the hypothesis reads F_R = p₁F_{R₁} + p₂F_{R₂} μ-a.e.; ‖β‖ is the operator norm of an n-covector β (a continuous alternating map).
1. The test form. ω ∈ TestFormOn U n is smooth, hence continuous, with compact support K := tsupport ω ⊆ U. A continuous function with compact support is bounded, so there is a real W with ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ W for every x (Mathlib Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support), and ω(x) = 0 for x ∉ K (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). K is compact, hence closed and Borel.
2. Unit orientations have norm at most one against covectors. If v is a unit orientation of a subspace Q, then v(β) = ±β(τ) for an orthonormal family τ, so |v(β)| = |β(τ)| ≤ ‖β‖·∏_i ‖τ_i‖ = ‖β‖ (Mathlib ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm, ‖τ_i‖ = 1).
3. Integrability on each carrier. Let R' = (M', θ', ξ') be any IMRep in U and h(x) := θ'(x)·ξ'(x)(ω(x)). (a) Measurability: x ↦ (θ'(x) : ℝ) is measurable (θ' is measurable and ℕ-valued), ξ' is a.e. strongly measurable for μ⌞M' (field aestronglyMeasurable_orient), ω is continuous, and the evaluation map Λ_n(ℝ^P) × Λⁿ(ℝ^P) → ℝ, (L, β) ↦ L(β), is continuous; hence h is a.e. strongly measurable for μ⌞M'. (b) Domination: by the field orients, μ⌞M'-a.e. ξ'(x) is a unit orientation of some subspace, so by step 2, for μ⌞M'-a.e. x: if x ∈ K then |h(x)| ≤ θ'(x)‖ω(x)‖ ≤ W·θ'(x), and if x ∉ K then ω(x) = 0 and h(x) = 0. Thus |h| ≤ W·1_K·θ' μ⌞M'-a.e. (c) The bound is integrable for μ⌞M': (μ⌞M')⌞K = μ⌞(K ∩ M') and ∫⁻_{M'∩K} θ' dμ < ∞ by the field locallyIntegrable_mult (K compact, K ⊆ U), so θ' is integrable for μ⌞(K ∩ M'), 1_K·θ' is integrable for μ⌞M' (integrable_indicator_iff) and so is W·1_K·θ'. By domination (Integrable.mono'), h is integrable for μ⌞M'.
4. Each action as a whole-space integral. For every x, F_{R'}(x)(ω(x)) = 1_{M'}(x)·h(x) (both vanish off M' and equal θ'(x)ξ'(x)(ω(x)) on M'). Since M' is Borel, R'.action ω = ∫_{M'} h dμ = ∫_{ℝ^P} F_{R'}(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) (integral_indicator), and x ↦ F_{R'}(x)(ω(x)) is μ-integrable by step 3 (integrable_indicator_iff). Apply this to R' = R, R₁, R₂.
5. Conclusion. Evaluation at a fixed covector is linear on Λ_n(ℝ^P): (a·L + b·L')(β) = a·L(β) + b·L'(β). Evaluating the hypothesis at β = ω(x) gives, for μ-a.e. x, F_R(x)(ω(x)) = p₁F_{R₁}(x)(ω(x)) + p₂F_{R₂}(x)(ω(x)). Integrals of μ-a.e. equal functions agree (integral_congr_ae), and the integral is linear on the integrable functions of step 4 (integral_add, integral_const_mul). Using step 4 three times: R.action ω = ∫ F_R(ω) dμ = p₁∫ F_{R₁}(ω) dμ + p₂∫ F_{R₂}(ω) dμ = p₁·R₁.action ω + p₂·R₂.action ω. Openness of U was not used. ∎
proof_key_steps: A test form is continuous, bounded by W and supported in the compact set K = tsupport ω ⊆ U.
On every carrier M', θ'ξ'(ω) is a.e. strongly measurable and dominated by W·1_K·θ', which is integrable by locallyIntegrable_mult.
R'.action ω = ∫ (1_{M'}θ'ξ')(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ(x) with an integrable integrand.
Evaluate the a.e. n-vector identity at ω(x), integrate and use linearity of the integral.

subproblems.title: Hausdorff measure of a blow-up inside a ball (scaling of H^n under η_{x,r})
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, x ∈ ℝ^P, r > 0, R ∈ ℝ and S ⊆ ℝ^P (arbitrary). With η_{x,r}(z) = r⁻¹(z − x) (SimonGMT Chapter03.blowUpMap x r) and H^n = μHE[n]: H^n(η_{x,r}(S) ∩ closedBall(0, R)) = (ENNReal.ofReal r)⁻¹^n · H^n(S ∩ closedBall(x, r·R)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (x : Euclid P) (r R : ℝ) (S : Set (Euclid P)), 0 < r → μHE[n] (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r '' S ∩ closedBall 0 R) = (ENNReal.ofReal r)⁻¹ ^ n * μHE[n] (S ∩ closedBall x (r * R))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the scaling identity Hⁿ(η_{y,r}(A Δ A') ∩ B_L(0)) = r^{−n}Hⁿ((A Δ A') ∩ B_{Lr}(y)) in step 3 (F2) of the supplied proof of the selected theorem (there justified by translation invariance and n-homogeneity of μHE[n]), here with closed balls; it is the identity Hⁿ(B_R(0) ∩ η_{x,λ}(M∖N_j)) = λ^{−n}Hⁿ(B_{λR}(x) ∩ M∖N_j) of Simon's proof of Ch. 3, Theorem 1.6 (chapter-03.txt lines 120–135). This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.regcomp_atl_blowUp_measure_scaling (DAG node root.regular_components_are_minimizing-a1.approx_tangent_locality-a1.blowup_measure_scaling-a1, candidate 0591fd7), reused at its byte-identical frozen type; the argument below is the one formalized there. Notation: η := η_{x,r}, μ := μHE[n]; r > 0 throughout.
1. Set identity. For every z, ‖η(z)‖ = |r⁻¹|·‖z − x‖ = r⁻¹‖z − x‖. Hence η(S) ∩ B̄_R(0) = η(S ∩ B̄_{rR}(x)): if y = η(z) with z ∈ S and ‖y‖ ≤ R, then ‖z − x‖ = r·(r⁻¹‖z − x‖) ≤ r·R, so z ∈ S ∩ B̄_{rR}(x); conversely, if z ∈ S and ‖z − x‖ ≤ rR, then ‖η(z)‖ = r⁻¹‖z − x‖ ≤ r⁻¹·(rR) = R. (For R < 0 both sides are empty.)
2. Decomposition of η. Let h := AffineMap.homothety x r⁻¹, so h(z) = r⁻¹·(z − x) + x, and let τ(y) := y + (−x). Then η(z) = τ(h(z)) for every z, hence η(T) = τ(h(T)) for every T ⊆ ℝ^P.
3. Scaling of μ. τ is an isometry of ℝ^P, so μ(τ(A)) = μ(A) for every A ⊆ ℝ^P (Mathlib Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image). For the homothety of ratio r⁻¹ ≠ 0, μ(h(T)) = ‖r⁻¹‖₊ⁿ·μ(T) for every T (Mathlib MeasureTheory.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image). Since r > 0, ‖r⁻¹‖₊ = ‖r‖₊⁻¹ with ‖r‖₊ = r, and its image in [0, ∞] is (ENNReal.ofReal r)⁻¹. Therefore μ(η(T)) = ((ENNReal.ofReal r)⁻¹)ⁿ·μ(T) for every T ⊆ ℝ^P.
4. Conclusion. By step 1 and step 3 with T := S ∩ B̄_{rR}(x): μ(η(S) ∩ B̄_R(0)) = μ(η(S ∩ B̄_{rR}(x))) = ((ENNReal.ofReal r)⁻¹)ⁿ·μ(S ∩ B̄_{rR}(x)). ∎
proof_key_steps: η_{x,r}(S) ∩ B̄_R(0) = η_{x,r}(S ∩ B̄_{rR}(x)) because ‖η_{x,r}(z)‖ = r⁻¹‖z − x‖.
η_{x,r} is the homothety of centre x and ratio r⁻¹ followed by the translation by −x.
Translations preserve μHE[n] and the homothety multiplies it by ‖r⁻¹‖₊ⁿ = ((ENNReal.ofReal r)⁻¹)ⁿ.
